description: The chosen a restores T, so R is A T V. c's written [T u] reads the synthetic T and predicts u strictly: only x → B, since x → ε cannot read. dt reads the same T as a bare terminal and predicts u in the ordinary way at the same position. The two predictions share the item of u. The ordinary step makes it ordinary, and the recognizer then predicts x in the ordinary way and lets u complete empty, so d is a second reading. A library that keeps an item strict once it has processed it as strict loses d and passes. Whether that library is caught depends on which prediction comes first, since strict and ordinary predictions share their items. This is reparse-strict-reclose with d listed before c. So one of the two cases catches it in any order of processing (engine §7.4).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%rule text a | b | d | c
%rule a A [+T] V
%rule b A [+T] [+T] V
%rule c A [+T u] W
%rule d A dt V
%rule dt T u
%rule u x
%rule x ε | B
